h1: The 8 Best Toaster Ovens for RVs of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Toaster Ovens for RVs: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 8 toaster ovens for RV galleys compared on size, wattage draw and safety features, from Elite Gourmet to Breville.
summary: The Elite Gourmet ETO449X is our top RV pick: it is marketed for RV use, draws 800W and has a cool-touch handle. If you want a bit more room, the Elite Gourmet ETO490 offers 9L and a 30 minute timer. For the smallest footprint, the ETO236 is a 2-slice squeeze. Only go for the 1800W Breville BOV650XL if your hookup or generator can carry the load.
intro: An RV galley has two hard limits that a house kitchen does not: counter space measured in inches and a power budget that a shared 30 amp or generator can run out of in a hurry. A toaster oven that looks tiny in a photo can still trip a breaker or refuse to fit a cabinet.

We reviewed eight toaster ovens across compact two-slice units and larger smart ovens. Each was ranked on how it uses space, what wattage it draws where the listing states it, and the safety details that matter when the kitchen moves. Where wattage is not listed, we say so.

products.name: Elite Gourmet ETO449X Toaster Oven
products.verdict: Marketed for RVs, 800W, compact 8.99L and a cool-touch handle. The sensible default.
products.description:
The ETO449X is explicitly marketed for RV use, with a stated 800W draw, a compact 8.99L cavity and a cool-touch handle that matters when the floor is shifting. It fits four slices and has a pizza function.

It beats the ETO490 on one number: 800W is gentler on a small generator, and the cavity is almost the same size. Compared with the Breville, it is far smaller but also far lighter on power. The trade is basic controls and no convection.

Buy it if you boondock or share a 30 amp circuit and want a toaster oven that suits the setup. Skip it if you cook for a crowd.
products.idealFor: RVers who need low wattage and a small footprint.
products.skipIf: You want convection or a big cavity.

products.name: Elite Gourmet ETO490 9L/4-Slice Oven
products.verdict: A 9L, 4-slice oven with a thermostat and 30 minute timer. Real baking in a tiny space.
products.description:
The ETO490 holds four slices in a 9L cavity, with a built-in thermostat to keep temperature steady and a 30 minute timer that is long enough for roasting and baking, not just toast.

It sits one rung behind the ETO449X because that model lists its 800W draw and RV marketing outright, while the ETO490 leaves wattage out of the summary. Against the 2-slice ETO236 it adds a longer timer and more room for a small pan.

A strong choice for RV cooks who want more than toast. Check the wattage on the listing before plugging it into a small inverter.
products.idealFor: RV cooks who want to bake as well as toast.
products.skipIf: Your power budget is tight and unconfirmed.

products.name: Elite Gourmet ETO236 Compact 2-Slice Toaster Oven
products.verdict: The smallest oven here, with a short 15 minute timer. Ideal for tiny galleys.
products.description:
The ETO236 is a compact 2-slice toaster oven with a built-in thermostat and a short 15 minute timer. It is the one that disappears into a cabinet most easily.

It trails the two bigger Elite Gourmet models because a 15 minute timer limits what you can cook, and two slices is fine for one or two people only. Compared with the Dash, it has a proper thermostat and a bit more room.

Pick it if counter space is the main constraint and you mostly reheat and toast. Do not expect to roast a meal.
products.idealFor: Couples and solo travelers with very little counter.
products.skipIf: You cook full meals in the RV.

products.name: Dash Mini Toaster Oven
products.verdict: Light, cheap and it shuts itself off. A reasonable small-space backup.
products.description:
The Dash Mini is a compact, light oven with a pizza function and an auto shutoff, which is a genuine safety plus in a moving vehicle. It is the least expensive pick in the roundup.

It ranks below the Elite Gourmet trio because their listings are more specific about thermostat and timer features. Against the ETO236 it trades a thermostat for the shutoff and a lower price.

A nice choice for a weekend camper who wants a cheap secondary cooker. Not for daily cooking.
products.idealFor: Weekend campers who want a cheap backup oven.
products.skipIf: You cook in your RV every day.

products.name: BLACK+DECKER 4-Slice Toaster Oven with Natural Convection
products.verdict: Four cooking modes and natural convection for a middle-of-the-road price.
products.description:
This BLACK+DECKER offers four cooking modes covering bake, broil, toast and warm, with natural convection to even out heat. It fits four slices and sits at a middle-ground price.

It ranks below the Elite Gourmet trio for RV use because its listing does not state a wattage, which makes power planning a guess. Compared with the TO1313SBD, it is the better-rounded option.

Best for RVers with a bigger rig who want more cooking range. Confirm the draw before relying on a generator.
cons: Bulkier than the Elite Gourmet picks
products.idealFor: Larger rigs where cooking variety matters.
products.skipIf: You run on a small inverter.

products.name: BLACK+DECKER TO1313SBD Toaster Oven
products.verdict: A curved interior that fits a 9-inch pizza or four slices. Roomy for the class.
products.description:
The TO1313SBD has a curved interior that fits a 9-inch pizza or four slices, which is more capacity than a basic 2-slice model. It also lists convection.

It lands below the other BLACK+DECKER because it is the older, plainer design, and it gives up the specific four-mode controls. It is larger than the Elite Gourmet picks, so cabinet fit is the question.

A good fit for a larger RV kitchen cooking for two or three people. Measure your counter before ordering.
products.idealFor: RV kitchens feeding two or three people.

products.name: Breville BOV450XL Mini Smart Oven
products.verdict: The smallest Breville with its five-quartz-element system. Premium, but costly.
products.description:
The BOV450XL is the smallest Breville in the lineup and uses the same five-quartz-element Element iQ system as larger models. Its stainless steel body is a step above the plastic competition.

It ranks lower for RV use because the price is several times the Elite Gourmet picks and the listing gives no wattage. It does beat the BOV650XL on counter space, since it is smaller.

Buy it if you live in the RV and want premium results. Check your power source first.
pros: Better fit for RV counters than larger Brevilles
products.idealFor: Full-timers who want premium results in a small body.
products.skipIf: You cook occasionally or run on a small generator.

products.name: Breville BOV650XL Compact Smart Oven
products.verdict: Fits a 12-inch pizza and preheats fast on 1800W. Great oven, hard on an RV.
products.description:
The BOV650XL fits a 12-inch pizza or a small roast, and its 1800W element preheats quickly. It uses the same Element iQ system as other Brevilles.

It finishes last because 1800W is a heavy draw for many RV hookups and generators, and the footprint is the largest here. Against the BOV450XL, it gives you more room at the cost of power and space.

Only buy it for a large rig on a strong shore power connection. Everyone else will fit better with an Elite Gourmet.
products.idealFor: Big rigs on stable shore power.
products.skipIf: You boondock or share a small generator.

whatMatters.detail: A toaster oven can draw anything from 800W to 1800W. A shared 30 amp circuit or a small inverter may not carry the bigger ones along with the air conditioner. Look for the wattage on the listing, and compare it with your generator or inverter rating before you buy.

whatMatters.factor: Measure the cabinet, not just the counter
whatMatters.detail: Many RV ovens live in a cabinet between uses. Measure width, depth and height, and leave a few inches behind and above for heat to escape. A unit that fits the counter in a photo may be too tall for the cabinet you plan to use.

In a moving RV, a hot door or handle is more dangerous than at home. Check for a cool-touch handle, an auto shutoff or a similar safety feature, and secure the oven whenever you drive, regardless of what the listing promises.

A 15 minute timer is fine for toast and reheating but too short for roasting. Look for 30 minutes or more if you plan to bake, and confirm the timer range in the product bullets rather than relying on a general description.

Convection moves air around the food so it cooks more evenly and often faster. It matters for baking and roasting, but basic toasting and reheating do not need it. Look for the word convection in the listing, and note that it may raise the price.

faq.q: How much power does a toaster oven use in an RV?
faq.a: It varies. The Elite Gourmet ETO449X lists 800W while the Breville BOV650XL lists 1800W. Check the wattage against your generator or inverter before buying.

faq.q: Can I run a toaster oven on an inverter?
faq.a: Only if the inverter can handle the wattage. A small unit like the ETO449X is a safer bet than a Breville BOV650XL. Always check the continuous rating.

faq.q: Is a convection toaster oven worth it in an RV?
faq.a: For baking and roasting, yes. For toast and reheating, no. Convection models like the BLACK+DECKER 4-Slice are bulkier, which can matter in a tiny galley.

faq.q: Do I need to secure a toaster oven when driving?
faq.a: Yes. Unplug it, let it cool and stow it in a cabinet or strap it down. A cool-touch handle helps, but it does not make it safe to leave loose.

faq.q: Is the Elite Gourmet ETO490 better than the ETO449X?
faq.a: The ETO490 has a 30 minute timer and a 9L cavity. The ETO449X lists 800W and RV marketing. Pick based on whether power or cooking time matters more.

faq.q: Can a toaster oven replace a microwave in an RV?
faq.a: For many meals, yes. It bakes, toasts and reheats, though it is slower for liquids. The ETO490 and Breville models are the most flexible here.

finalTake: For most RVers the Elite Gourmet ETO449X is the right answer: RV marketing, 800W and a cool-touch handle. Want more cooking time? The Elite Gourmet ETO490 has a 30 minute timer. Tiny galley? Take the ETO236. Only pick the Breville BOV650XL if your rig has strong shore power, because 1800W is a lot to ask of a small system.
